sql.sqlStatement: Specify the workbook containing the data
SET DATA FILE
Clear the 'data' worksheet
RESET

Exaple 1 - Build Continent nodes, where each node lists all the Countries in the Continent using the RECTANGLE shape. The fields emitted to the data worksheet are specified in the first SQL statement [SQL FOR ID]. (NOTE:The SQL passed as parameters has been kept to one line to reduce confusion).

SELECT 
  TRUE                                                     AS [ITERATE],
  'SELECT DISTINCT [ContinentCode] AS [ID], [continent] AS [Item], [Continent] AS [External Label], [Continent] AS [Label], ''Rectangle'' AS [Style Name] FROM [countries$]' 
                                                           AS [SQL FOR ID],
  'SELECT [Country] AS [Label] FROM [countries$] WHERE [ContinentCode] = ''{ID}'' AND [ContinentCode] IS NOT NULL'                                 
                                                           AS [SQL FOR DATA],
  TRUE                                                     AS [CONCATENATE],
  'Label'                                                  AS [FIELD],
  'Label'                                                  AS [ASSIGN TO], 
  ''                                                       AS [PREFIX], 
  ''                                                       AS [SUFFIX], 
  '\n'                                                     AS [SEPARATOR]

Example 2: Build Continent nodes, where each node lists all the Countries in the Continent using the RECORD shape. The fields emitted to the data worksheet are specified in the first SQL statement [SQL FOR ID]. (NOTE:The SQL passed as parameters has been kept to one line to reduce confusion).

SELECT 
  TRUE                                                     AS [ITERATE],
  'SELECT DISTINCT [ContinentCode] AS [ID], [continent] AS [Item], [Continent] AS [External Label], [Continent] AS [Label], ''Record'' AS [Style Name] FROM [countries$]' 
                                                           AS [SQL FOR ID],
  'SELECT [Country] AS [Label] FROM [countries$] WHERE [ContinentCode] = ''{ID}'' AND [ContinentCode] IS NOT NULL'                                 
                                                           AS [SQL FOR DATA],
  TRUE                                                     AS [CONCATENATE],
  'Label'                                                  AS [FIELD],
  'Label'                                                  AS [ASSIGN TO], 
  '{'                                                      AS [PREFIX], 
  '}'                                                      AS [SUFFIX], 
  '|'                                                      AS [SEPARATOR]
Preview / Publish the graphs
PREVIEW
PUBLISH
Quick Help
Excel SQL Syntax
https://exceltographviz.com/sql/syntax/
Clear the 'data' worksheet
RESET
Turn on/off logging of errors to file 'Relationship Visualizer ADO Log.txt'
ENABLE LOGGING
DISABLE LOGGING
Write environment diagonostic information to file 'Relationship Visualizer ADO Log.txt'
LOG ENVIRONMENT
Specify the workbook containing the data
SET DATA FILE
Create the edges

SELECT [From Column] AS [Item], 
       [To Column]   AS [Related Item] 
FROM   [Worksheet Name$]
Create the nodes

SELECT [Node Id Column]    AS [Item],
       [Node Label Column] AS [Label],
       [Node Style Column] AS [Style Name]
FROM   [Worksheet Name$] 
WHERE  ...
Create edges which chain a set of nodes

SELECT [Node Id Column] AS [ITEM], 
       TRUE             AS [CREATE EDGES]
FROM   [Worksheet Name$]
WHERE  ...
Create a subgraph, with rank= constraint specified as either 'same' | 'min' | 'source' | 'max' | 'sink'.

The rank attribute tells Graphviz how to line up the nodes inside a subgraph:
- rank=same   - all nodes sit on the same horizontal (or vertical) level.
- rank=min    - all nodes are pushed to the top (or left) of the graph.
- rank=source - same as min, but Graphviz also ensures that only subgraphs marked source or min share that top/left rank.
- rank=max    - all nodes are pushed to the bottom (or right) of the graph.
- rank=sink   - same as max, but restricted to subgraphs marked sink or max.
NOTE: Graphviz treats the minimum rank as the top/left edge of the layout and the maximum rank as the bottom/right edge.

SELECT [Node Id Column] AS [ITEM], 
       TRUE             AS [CREATE RANK],
       'same'           AS [RANK]
FROM   [Worksheet Name$]
WHERE  ...
Split text for labels at first blank after 10 characters

SELECT [Label Column] AS [Label],
       10             AS [SPLIT LENGTH],
       ...
Specify the line ending (\l, \n, \r, | etc.) to use when splitting a label

SELECT [Label Column] AS [Label],
       10             AS [SPLIT LENGTH],
       '\r'           AS [LINE ENDING],
       ...
Group nodes into a cluster

SELECT [Cluster Id Column]         AS [CLUSTER],
       [Cluster Label Column]      AS [CLUSTER LABEL],
       [Cluster Style Name Column] AS [CLUSTER STYLE NAME],
       [Cluster Attributes]        AS [CLUSTER ATTRIBUTES],
       [Cluster Tooltip Column]    AS [CLUSTER TOOLTIP],
       [Node Id Column]            AS [Item],
       [Node Label Column]         AS [Label],
       [Node Style Name Column]    AS [Style Name],
       ...
Group nodes into two level clusters

SELECT [Outer Cluster Id Column]         AS [CLUSTER],
       [Outer Cluster Label Column]      AS [CLUSTER LABEL],
       [Outer Cluster Style Name Column] AS [CLUSTER STYLE NAME],
       [Outer Cluster Attributes]        AS [CLUSTER ATTRIBUTES],
       [Outer Cluster Tooltip Column]    AS [CLUSTER TOOLTIP],

       [Inner Cluster Id Column]         AS [SUBCLUSTER],
       [Inner Cluster Label Column]      AS [SUBCLUSTER LABEL],
       [Inner Cluster Style Name Column] AS [SUBCLUSTER STYLE NAME],
       [Inner Cluster Attributes]        AS [SUBCLUSTER ATTRIBUTES],
       [Inner Cluster Tooltip Column]    AS [SUBCLUSTER TOOLTIP],

       [Node Id Column]                  AS [Item],
       [Node Label Column]               AS [Label],
       [Node Style Name Column]          AS [Style Name],
       ...

Loop count substitution strings (useful in sortv= attributes, style names, and labels). 
  {clc} = Cluster count
  {scc} = Subcluster count
  {rsc} = Record set count

SELECT 'sortv={clc}'    AS [CLUSTER ATTRIBUTES],
       'Border {clc} '  AS [CLUSTER STYLE NAME],
       'sortv={scc}'    AS [SUBCLUSTER ATTRIBUTES],
       'sortv={rsc}'    AS [Attributes],
       ...
FROM   [Worksheet Name$] 
WHERE  ...
ORDER BY [Outer Cluster Label Column] ASC,
         [Inner Cluster Label Column] ASC,
         [Node Label Column]          ASC
Show the graph immediately after all SQL statements processed
PREVIEW [ AS ( DIRECTED | UNDIRECTED ) GRAPH ]
Publish graphs as files
PUBLISH [ ALL VIEWS ] [ AS ( DIRECTED | UNDIRECTED ) GRAPH ] [ file prefix ]

buttons.screenTip: Describes the attributes used by various Graphviz tools
buttons.superTip: The table gives the name of the attribute, the graph components (node, edge, etc.) which use the attribute and the type of the attribute (strings representing legal values of that type). Where applicable, the table also gives a default value for the attribute, a minimum allowed setting for numeric attributes, and certain restrictions on the use of the attribute.
